gloss: to fray; to come unstitched; to come loose

definitions.explanation: Of a seam, hem, or woven edge, to come apart so that the threads loosen and hang out.
Of hair that is tied up, for strands to come loose and hang down.

examples.japanese: ⟦セーター→セーター：01371_seetaa⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{裾|すそ}→裾：06488_suso⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ほつれて⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: The hem of the sweater is coming unravelled.

examples.japanese: ⟦{長|なが}く→長い：00491_nagai⟧⟦{使|つか}った→使う：00473_tsukau⟧⟦かばん→かばん：00637_kaban⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{縫|ぬ}い{目|め}→縫い目：07102_nuime⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ほつれてきた⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦{自分|じぶん}→自分：02887_jibun⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{縫|ぬ}い{直|なお}した。
examples.english: The seams of my old bag were starting to come apart, so I sewed them up myself.

examples.japanese: {結|ゆ}った⟦{髪|かみ}→髪：02196_kami⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{少|すこ}し→少し：00596_sukoshi⟧ほつれて⟦いた→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: A few strands had come loose from her tied-up hair.

examples.japanese: ⟦{風|かぜ}→風：00641_kaze⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{吹|ふ}かれて→吹く：02445_fuku⟧、⟦まとめた→まとめる：02424_matomeru⟧⟦{髪|かみ}→髪：02196_kami⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ほつれて⟦{顔|かお}→顔：00558_kao⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦かかった→かかる：00711_kakaru⟧。
examples.english: In the wind, strands came loose from her gathered hair and fell across her face.

notes:
Written {綻|ほつ}れる in kanji, but usually in kana.

ASPECT (ている):
ほつれて⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧ describes the frayed state: ⟦{裾|すそ}→裾：06488_suso⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ほつれて⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧ (the hem is frayed).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{縫|ぬ}い{目|め}→縫い目：07102_nuime⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ほつれる: a seam comes apart
- ⟦{裾|すそ}→裾：06488_suso⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ほつれる: a hem frays
- ほつれ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{直|なお}す / ⟦{繕|つくろ}う→繕う：11066_tsukurou⟧: to mend a frayed spot (ほつれ, the noun)

WATCH OUT:
⟦{綻|ほころ}びる→綻びる：07660_hokorobiru⟧, written with the same kanji, also means to come unstitched, and is used of buds opening and faces breaking into smiles.
